summary.headline: Moneyboxx Q2 FY27 PAT rose to INR0.9 crore (+229% YoY) as October disbursements crossed INR50 crore; AUM guided to INR1,100-1,200 crore by March 2027.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 disbursements were INR87 crore, up 14% QoQ from INR76 crore in Q1, and monthly disbursements rose from INR24.5 crore in August to INR32.4 crore in September and above INR50 crore in October 2026. Total income was INR61 crore (+11% YoY, +17% QoQ) and pre-provisioning operating profit was INR9.97 crore (+79% YoY), while PAT was INR0.9 crore. AUM stood at INR802 crore at September 2026, with 90+ PAR down to 2.56% from 6.25% in March 2026, helped by ARC transactions. Management is steering to H2 disbursements of INR500-600 crore and AUM of INR1,100-1,200 crore by March 2027, with four growth engines (MSME, livestock, rooftop solar, digital lending) and partnerships now contributing.

financial_highlights.value: INR24.5 crore (Aug 2026), INR32.4 crore (Sep 2026), above INR50 crore (Oct 2026)
financial_highlights.change: More than doubled in two months

segments.name: Core MSME lending
segments.commentary: Secured loans of INR3-30 lakh and unsecured loans to CIBIL-qualified borrowers of INR1-3 lakh; 148 branches across 12 states, ~13,000 live customers. Branch secured MSME is improving slowly; secured TAT down to 6.5-7 days from 10-11 days.

segments.name: Livestock and dairy finance
segments.commentary: Partnership with Akshayakalpa started in Q2 with FLDG cover; partner handles collections. Disbursements in September were about INR30 lakh.

segments.name: Rooftop solar finance
segments.commentary: AUM about INR17 crore in H1 (cited as INR22.5 crore after October); disbursed INR5.5 crore in October vs INR27 lakh in April. Yield about 22.7%, with 10% second-loss guarantee (first loss capped at 3%). Target INR25 crore per month and renewable loans ~10% of AUM within a year.

segments.name: Digital lending (SmartBiz via Bachatt/Trusave)
segments.commentary: Launched in Q2 with Bachatt as lending service provider and FLDG cover; about INR2 crore disbursed in late September, INR2 crore in October, with a target of at least INR5 crore for November.

guidance_outlook: H2 FY27 disbursement target of INR500-600 crore, implying AUM of INR1,100-1,200 crore by March 2027.

Long-term goal of monthly disbursements of INR100 crore, referencing FY24 run-rate of INR75 crore and Jan-Mar 2026 average of INR100 crore; management said November cannot jump from INR50 crore to INR100 crore.
Opex to average AUM targeted below 10% within two years, from 14.3% in H1 FY27.
Borrowing costs up 25-30 bps in MSME funding; bank funding expected to stay competitive. Management sees funding as adequate for the next 2-3 quarters.
Partnership-sourced disbursements of about INR30 crore per month expected in the next quarter, with Loom at minimum INR10 crore per month by January 2027.
capex_capacity: 148 branches across 12 states as of September 2026; management focused on branch productivity rather than new footprint.
Moneyboxx ONE LOS launched May 2026; Cattle AI reduces manual screening effort by 30-40%; MBCollect supports field collections; in-house app due for launch at end of November 2026.
Opex stable in absolute terms; growth targeted without proportionate fixed-cost increase.
Possible first-loss guarantee for rooftop solar and CGFMU guarantee revival cited as likely near-term, not confirmed.
demand_pricing: Existing-customer top-up lending restarted late September 2026 (INR15 crore in October) after about 18 months of pause following MFI guardrails; 1 lakh+ past customers, many with strong repayment records.
Unsecured lending spread of 17-18% and secured spread of about 10%, per management, which links profitability to AUM growth.
Management said lending IRR moderation reflects shift to higher-ticket secured book, with IRR rising QoQ as existing-customer and higher-CIBIL unsecured lending starts.
Management is not pursuing co-lending or VC funding at present.

qa_highlights.question: How comfortable is funding after INR110 crore of NCDs in Q2, and what is the outlook on borrowing costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Liquidity is INR170 crore at September; 36 lenders including 12 banks, with Bandhan Bank newly added and IOB topping up. MSME borrowing costs are up 25-30 bps, while bank funding is expected to stay competitive. Management sees no funding constraint for 2-3 quarters even with 50-70% AUM growth.

qa_highlights.question: Any material regulatory changes after the middle-layer NBFC classification?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said nothing material; some additional compliance requirements and an auditor change, but no significant impact on normal operations.

qa_highlights.question: What are the H2 FY27 priorities for disbursement, AUM, asset quality and profitability?
qa_highlights.answer: AUM growth is the priority with opex broadly fixed. Target is INR500-600 crore disbursements in H2 for AUM of INR1,100-1,200 crore. Existing-customer lending restarted (INR15 crore in October), NPA collections reportedly tripled from September, and SARFAESI actions have started.

qa_highlights.question: What is the sustainable monthly disbursement run rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is INR100 crore per month as soon as possible; management said it cannot go from INR50 crore in October to INR100 crore in November. Partnerships could add about INR30 crore per month, and management cited FY24 at INR75 crore per month.

qa_highlights.question: What scale can partnerships reach by March 2027?
qa_highlights.answer: Loom is expected to reach at least INR10 crore per month by January 2027; Bachatt could reach INR20 crore per month from January if digital lending takes off. Management flagged execution risk and gave no firm total.

qa_highlights.question: What is the growth plan, yield and credit risk for rooftop solar versus core MSME?
qa_highlights.answer: Target is INR25 crore per month. Yield is about 22.7% (current 23-23.5%). OEM-sourced leads lower opex, a 10% second-loss guarantee caps first loss at 3%, and funding is a 4-year tenor, limiting ALM mismatch.

risks_watch: Execution risk on the H2 target of INR500-600 crore disbursements and INR1,100-1,200 crore AUM by March 2027, versus AUM of INR802 crore at September 2026.
Reliance on partnerships and FLDG/guarantee cover (Akshayakalpa, Bachatt, Loom, solar OEMs); management said execution issues are possible and first-loss guarantee for solar is not yet confirmed.

Collection efficiency of 92.5% overall (above 98% ex-bucket) and reported gross NPA of 0.01% partly reflect ARC transactions; underlying asset quality needs watching as existing-customer lending resumes.
Lending yield moderation (IRR 24.8% H1) with higher-ticket secured mix; opex/AUM at 14.3% is high until AUM scales.
Borrowing costs up 25-30 bps in MSME funding; funding dependence on NCDs (46% of borrowings).
Profitability is thin: Q2 PAT INR0.9 crore; the 229% YoY growth is off a low base.
Transcript inconsistencies: the Q2 PAT growth and some AUM figures (e.g., INR1,000-1,200 crore) were restated in the call; the 'Q1 INR87 crore' secured-share remark is unclear.
key_quotes: From 50, I cannot go to 100 in November. But we are actually expecting a very strong growth going forward.
It's difficult to comment right now. We have our internal targets, but there could be some issues in terms of execution and all.
So, it's a 4-year stable kind of lending.
So broadly, we don't see funding as a concern as of now.
Even we have to grow it to 50% to 70%, I think funding will not be a concern.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on disbursement momentum, partnerships and asset quality, citing October disbursements above INR50 crore and collections improving. It was cautious and evasive on partnership scale by March 2027 ("difficult to comment", "still yet to be seen") and on the 100 crore monthly run rate, and it acknowledged execution risk.

growth.why: Management guides H2 FY27 disbursements of INR500-600 crore and March 2027 AUM of INR1,100-1,200 crore (vs AUM INR802 crore in Sep 2026), backed by October disbursements above INR50 crore, partnerships (Akshayakalpa, Loom, Bachatt) and rooftop solar and digital lending ramp-ups, but no committed capacity or contracted orders with numbers, so backing is only partial.

rows.label: Margin expansion

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: 148 branches across 12 states with management focused on branch productivity rather than new footprint, so no new branch capacity is planned in the window.

rows.label: Volume growth

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: No utilisation metric is disclosed, and no capex is guided; only a possible first-loss guarantee for rooftop solar (capped at 3%) and CGFMU revival are cited as near-term, unconfirmed.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management is cautious on partnership scale and the INR100 crore monthly run rate, saying November cannot jump from INR50 crore to INR100 crore, so no upgrade is signalled.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: H2 disbursement target of INR500-600 crore needs about INR83-100 crore per month versus INR50 crore+ in October, and AUM must rise from INR802 crore to INR1,100-1,200 crore by March 2027; management flagged partnership execution risk and cannot say whether Loom or Bachatt will scale.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: In-house app is due for launch at end of November 2026, and digital lending (SmartBiz via Bachatt) launched in Q2 with about INR2 crore disbursed in October and a target of at least INR5 crore for November.

rows.label: Partnership-sourced disbursements of about INR30 crore per month
rows.why: Management expects about INR30 crore per month from partnerships next quarter, with Loom at minimum INR10 crore per month by January 2027, though no firm total was given.

rows.label: Rooftop solar scale-up to INR25 crore per month
rows.why: Rooftop solar disbursed INR5.5 crore in October versus INR27 lakh in April, with a target of INR25 crore per month and renewable loans around 10% of AUM within a year.

rows.label: Funding adequacy for 2-3 quarters
rows.why: Liquidity is INR170 crore, with 36 lenders and NCDs at 46% of borrowings, and management sees no funding constraint even with 50-70% AUM growth, though MSME borrowing costs are up 25-30 bps.

tone.note: Management was confident on October disbursements above INR50 crore, collections and partnerships, but cautious on partnership scale by March 2027 and on the INR100 crore monthly run rate; analysts pushed on funding costs, regulatory changes and the H2 target path.
